# Poisson equations and changing parameters {#sec-poisson-feedback}

The frozen augmented process has a stationary law $\nu_\theta$ and, under @thm-wasserstein-lifting, geometric Wasserstein contraction. For the controlled recursion, the remaining question is whether the centred observation can be accumulated along a path on which $\theta$ changes. We work with Lipschitz functions throughout; no weighted total-variation convergence of the augmented process is assumed.

## Frozen Poisson equation on the Lipschitz space

For a scalar observable $G_\theta\in\operatorname{Lip}(\mathsf Z,d_Z)$, put

$$
F(\theta)=\nu_\theta(G_\theta),\qquad
\bar G_\theta=G_\theta-F(\theta).
$$ {#eq-centred-adam-observable}

Vector-valued observables are handled coordinatewise. Consider the frozen Poisson equation

$$
u_\theta-Q_\theta u_\theta=\bar G_\theta.
$$ {#eq-augmented-poisson}

Under geometric Wasserstein contraction, finite first eccentricity and the corresponding first-moment conditions, [@Hofstadler2026, Theorem 3.4] applies to this centred Lipschitz observable. In particular, a solution is given by

$$
u_\theta(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty Q_\theta^n\bar G_\theta(z),
$$ {#eq-poisson-series}

with $\nu_\theta(u_\theta)=0$ and

$$
\|u_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}
\leq\Lambda_\theta\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)},
\qquad
\Lambda_\theta:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)
\leq\frac{C_Z(\eta)}{1-\eta}.
$$ {#eq-poisson-lipschitz-bound}

The series and its normalisation are understood in the integrable Lipschitz class supplied by the theorem. The regularity assumption concerns the *forcing observable* $G_\theta$, not only the memory update $T_\theta$. The square-root coordinates and bounded-innovation case of @eq-sqrt-memory-update--@eq-adam-readout-lipschitz give one direct verification for Adam's normalised readout.

## Parameter differences of Poisson solutions

The one-step estimate @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound is sufficient for the invariant-law perturbation argument. It is not, by itself, an estimate of the Lipschitz seminorm of $(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f$ as a function of the state. We therefore record explicitly the additional operator condition used in the following restricted-space result.

::: {#asm-poisson-operator}
## Lipschitz-space operator regularity

On $\mathsf K$ suppose the quantities $\Lambda_\theta$ in @eq-poisson-lipschitz-bound are uniformly bounded by $\Lambda<\infty$, and that

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}&\leq L_G,\\
\|G_\theta-G_\vartheta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
&\leq L_{G,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|,\\
\|(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
&\leq L_{\mathrm{op}}\|\theta-\vartheta\|
\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-poisson-operator-assumption}

for every Lipschitz $f$. The seminorm of a constant is zero, so the last inequality is unaffected by adding constants to $f$. Assume the corresponding Poisson solutions are well defined, as above.
:::

This is an explicit sufficient hypothesis, not a consequence claimed from @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound. It can be replaced by a weaker weighted resolvent estimate if such an estimate is verified directly. The approach parallels the parameter-dependent Poisson argument of [@Care2026], formulated there in a weighted sup-norm rather than the present Lipschitz seminorm.

::: {#prp-poisson-parameter}
## Parameter regularity in the restricted Lipschitz space

Under @asm-poisson-operator, fix $z_0\in\mathsf Z$ and choose the normalisation $u_\theta(z_0)=0$ for every $\theta\in\mathsf K$. Then

$$
\|u_\theta-u_\vartheta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}
\leq\Lambda\left(L_{G,\theta}
+L_{\mathrm{op}}\Lambda L_G\right)\|\theta-\vartheta\|.
$$ {#eq-poisson-parameter-lipschitz}

In particular,

$$
|u_\theta(z)-u_\vartheta(z)|
\leq\Lambda\left(L_{G,\theta}
+L_{\mathrm{op}}\Lambda L_G\right)
\|\theta-\vartheta\|d_Z(z,z_0).
$$ {#eq-poisson-parameter-pointwise}
:::

::: {.proof}
Subtract the two Poisson equations, writing $v=u_\theta-u_\vartheta$:

$$
(I-Q_\theta)v=
(G_\theta-G_\vartheta)
-\bigl(F(\theta)-F(\vartheta)\bigr)
+(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)u_\vartheta.
$$ {#eq-poisson-parameter-identity}

The right-hand side has zero $\nu_\theta$-mean: this follows by integrating the identity against $\nu_\theta$ and using invariance. Its Lipschitz seminorm is at most

$$
\left(L_{G,\theta}
+L_{\mathrm{op}}\|u_\vartheta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\right)
\|\theta-\vartheta\|.
$$

The frozen Poisson estimate @eq-poisson-lipschitz-bound, applied to this centred right-hand side, bounds the Lipschitz seminorm of its solution by $\Lambda$ times the displayed quantity. Use $\|u_\vartheta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq\Lambda L_G$ to obtain @eq-poisson-parameter-lipschitz. Solutions of the centred Poisson equation differ by constants; the common value at $z_0$ identifies $v$ with the normalised solution. The pointwise estimate follows by the definition of the Lipschitz seminorm.
:::

The distinction between @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound and @eq-poisson-operator-assumption matters for the intended application. The first has already been reduced to driver-level parameter estimates. The second still requires verification, or an alternative weighted resolvent argument, before the stated Poisson parameter conclusion can be invoked.

## The feedback term in the controlled recursion

Return to the changing-parameter augmented process,

$$
Z_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n\sim Q_{\theta_n}(Z_n,\cdot),
\qquad
\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+\gamma_{n+1}G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1}).
$$ {#eq-augmented-controlled-sa}

For Adam, $G_\theta$ is the normalised readout on the augmented memory. The order of the transition and parameter update in @eq-augmented-controlled-sa is the one used in @eq-adam-recursion. Define

$$
\Delta M_{n+1}
=u_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-Q_{\theta_n}u_{\theta_n}(Z_n).
$$ {#eq-poisson-martingale-increment}

Then $\mathbb E[\Delta M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0$. Put $\phi_\theta=Q_\theta u_\theta$. Evaluating @eq-augmented-poisson at $Z_{n+1}$ and adding and subtracting $\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)$ gives

$$
G_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-F(\theta_n)
=\Delta M_{n+1}
+\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_n)-\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1}).
$$ {#eq-controlled-poisson-decomposition}

Under weighted summation, the last two terms telescope except for boundary, gain-variation and parameter-change terms. The latter involve

$$
\phi_{\theta_n}(Z_{n+1})-
\phi_{\theta_{n+1}}(Z_{n+1}).
$$ {#eq-poisson-feedback-remainder}

The operator decomposition

$$
\phi_\theta-\phi_\vartheta
=(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)u_\theta+
Q_\vartheta(u_\theta-u_\vartheta)
$$ {#eq-poisson-feedback-operator}
 
shows how @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound and @prp-poisson-parameter enter together. If these differences have the required weighted growth bound, and $\|\theta_{n+1}-\theta_n\|=O(\gamma_{n+1})$, the parameter-change remainder is of second order after multiplication by the SA gain. Controlling the sum still requires integrability along the adaptive path.

The standard Poisson--martingale method of controlled stochastic approximation [@BenvenisteMetivierPriouret1990; @AndrieuMoulines2006; @Care2026] then suggests the limiting equation

$$
\dot\theta=F(\theta).
$$ {#eq-adam-limiting-ode}

No asymptotic pseudo-trajectory or parameter-convergence theorem is claimed here. Such a theorem additionally requires a stability or localisation argument for $(\theta_n)$, a gain condition, martingale moment estimates and control of the weighted remainders in @eq-controlled-poisson-decomposition. The preceding results identify the precise frozen and parameter-dependent estimates that would enter that proof; they do not replace it.
